svg.title: City layers to the act of nesting and our plot
svg.text: ENTERING BEIRUT / LAYERS → NESTING
CONCEPT STUDY / 02
From layers beside each other to layers belonging together.
The city gives us the conditions. Nesting changes how we bring them together on our plot.
01 / READ THE CITY
EXISTING CONDITIONS · APPROVED DRAWING RETAINED
Street 52 → C1 crossing and stairs → our plot-side arrival → Street 80 → Seaside Road.
The crossing already exists. We translate the changes in scale, enclosure and continuity—not the city’s shapes.
02 / THE ACT OF NESTING
A proposed spatial operation. Coloured ribbons are relationships—not walls or building masses.
A / SEPARATE
Different conditions sit beside each other.
A route alone does not make them shared.
B / NEST
Let one setting hold a smaller one.
The interval between them becomes a place.
C / CONNECT
Keep openings through the layers.
Belong together without becoming identical.
Not seven rings for seven city conditions: a change from separation to connected, nested settings.
03 / REFLECT THE OPERATION ON OUR PLOT
Actual boundary + the compact envelope test. Ribbons and approach arrows are proposed relationships.
N
OPEN GROUND
Arrival stays outside first.
The whole plot is not roofed.
SOUTH / AFTER THE C1 STAIRS
The arrival becomes a place to pause,
then passes through connected layers.
EAST / STREET 80
A separate walk-in joins
the same shared welcome.
EAST VEHICLES → B1
Separate parking approach.
Ramp not designed here.
1 / HOLD THE ARRIVAL
A threshold receives the southern approach.
It is more than a line at the door.
2 / MAKE THE IN-BETWEEN SHARED
The space between layers gives people
somewhere to meet, pause and orient.
3 / NEST WITHOUT CUTTING OFF
Smaller settings remain within that shared
world, reached through visible openings.
Solid outline: source plot · Dashed inset: study clearance · Dotted rectangle: tested envelope
“I take the layers from the city, but change their relationship on our plot.”
“Instead of only passing from one condition to another, people enter a shared setting that holds smaller ones.
That is nesting: each layer keeps its character, while the spaces and openings between them bring them together.”
Concept test, not selected massing. 408 m² envelope retained (27.4% of the plot); abstract ribbon heights are not storeys.
Final footprint, program, stair-landing connection, step-free arrival, B1 and ramp geometry remain VERIFY.
